theme: 3 terms on writing tidy Swift: choosing a value in one line, filtering a loop and running cleanup code later

terms.definition: An operator that picks one of two values by checking a condition, written as `condition ? a : b`.
terms.example: Use ternary operators for short choices like `Pass` or `Retry`.
terms.code:
let score = 8
let result = score > 5 ? "Pass" : "Retry"
print(result)

terms.definition: A condition added to a loop or pattern that keeps only the items matching it.
terms.example: Use where clauses to loop over only the scores above 4.

terms.definition: A statement that holds code to run later, when the current scope is about to end.
terms.example: Use defers to close the file, even if the function returns early.

video.description:
Learn to talk about tidy Swift code: Ternary Operator, Where Clause & Defer, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Ternary Operator - An operator that picks one of two values by checking a condition, written as `condition ? a : b`.
Where Clause - A condition added to a loop or pattern that keeps only the items matching it.
Defer - A statement that holds code to run later, when the current scope is about to end.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Ternary Operator, Where Clause & Defer in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
삼항 연산자, Where 절, Defer 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Ternary Operator - An operator that picks one of two values by checking a condition, written as `condition ? a : b`.
한국어: 삼항 연산자: 조건에 따라 두 값 중 하나를 고르는 연산자

Where Clause - A condition added to a loop or pattern that keeps only the items matching it.
한국어: Where 절: 반복문이나 패턴에 조건을 붙여 맞는 항목만 남기는 구문

Defer - A statement that holds code to run later, when the current scope is about to end.
한국어: Defer: 현재 범위가 끝나기 직전에 실행할 코드를 미리 등록하는 문

dialogue.title: Tidy code in a chat

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, my loop shows a label for every `score` in `scores`, but zero is not real data.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Add a Where Clause. With `where score > 0`, the loop skips zero.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the Where Clause filters the items before the loop body runs?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Now for the label, use a Ternary Operator instead of a long if.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm, is a Ternary Operator better than an if?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For two short values, yes. `score > 5 ? "high" : "low"` is easy to read.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I see. Oh no, I forgot to print Done when `show` ends.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use Defer at the top. Defer runs its code when the function is about to end.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Even if the function returns early?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, that is why Defer is great for cleanup.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. Where Clause to filter, Ternary Operator to choose, Defer to clean up.
Use ternary operators for short choices.
